Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and reduced
range of motion. Over the course of 25 visits, care consisted of spinal mobilization, soft tissue therapy, therapeutic
exercise, and home stretching program instruction. The reported neck injury is consistent in type and severity with the
mechanism of the collision as described. Treatment progressed along a typical clinical trajectory, with visit frequency
tapering as symptoms improved and function returned. Examination revealed palpable paraspinal muscle tenderness
and restricted cervical rotation that support the persence of a soft tissue injury; neurological screening, reflexes, and
strength testing were within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the cervical region is known to this provider.
Billed services correspond to the documented visits, with no duplicate or repeated charges identified. Patient was
discharged from active care with a home exercise plan and instructions to return if symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
